questions.prompt: How much classical information can superdense coding transmit using one qubit and one pre-shared entangled pair?
questions.explanation: Superdense coding transmits 2 classical bits using one qubit transmission plus pre-shared entanglement — twice the capacity of an unentangled qubit.

questions.prompt: What resource cost does quantum teleportation require to transmit one qubit's worth of information?
options: One shared entangled pair and 2 classical bits of communication
Only a classical bit, no entanglement needed
questions.explanation: Teleportation consumes one shared entangled pair and requires transmitting 2 classical bits to convey one qubit's quantum information.

questions.prompt: Why does no-cloning force quantum communication protocols to be designed around 'consuming' entanglement resources?
options: Because quantum information cannot be copied, so it must be consumed/used directly rather than amplified or duplicated
Classical communication has the same restriction
questions.explanation: Since quantum information can't be copied, protocols must consume entanglement resources directly rather than duplicating signals as classical systems do.

questions.prompt: What is a key advantage of satellite-based quantum communication over pure fiber-based approaches?
options: Satellites have no distance limitations at all
Free-space links avoid the cumulative photon loss of long fiber runs, enabling longer-range entanglement distribution
questions.explanation: Satellite links avoid cumulative fiber photon loss, enabling demonstrated longer-range entanglement distribution than fiber alone currently achieves.

questions.prompt: What two metrics determine a real quantum communication system's performance?
questions.explanation: Entanglement distribution rate (pairs generated per second) and fidelity (closeness to perfect entanglement) are the key performance metrics.
